question: Which counties nationwide should Punctual Pros expand to first?
html:
Where Punctual Pros Should Expand First

Expand first into the counties next to the Central-PA core and the Jersey Shore beachhead, not into new national markets. The named targets point to Chester County, PA, New Castle County, DE, and Monmouth, Middlesex, Somerset, Union and Essex counties, NJ, with Worcester County, MD as a second step.

Why stay close to home

  • In the plan, Phase 1 (months 0-12) fills the 248-zip core and the 195 best nearby ZIP codes: 144 in PA and 51 in MD (Punctual Pros nationwide plan).
  • Phase 2 (months 9-24) repeats the Horvath deal across PA, NJ, MD, DE and southern NY. That region holds 54 mapped Authority territories Punctual Pros does not yet own (Punctual Pros nationwide plan).
  • Across sponsor cases, the first add-on came early and close to home, a median of about 7 months after entry. Tuck-ins then followed every three to five months (value creation cases).
  • A national move comes last. Phase 4 means consolidating inside the One Hour / Ben Franklin / Mister Sparky system, where Punctual Pros holds about 2.3% of $831M reported revenue (Punctual Pros nationwide plan).

(Punctual Pros add-on targets)

  • The Ron Williams group owns both West Chester and Delmarva. One deal could open Chester and Worcester counties (est.).
  • Phase 3 metros come after these: Baltimore-DC, Richmond, the Philadelphia suburbs and Pittsburgh (Punctual Pros nationwide plan).

What the data cannot yet show

  • The national county table was generated Oct 6, 2026, but the context does not include its county rankings. A true nationwide ranking needs its demand, climate and Authority-density fields sorted by score.
  • Connecticut cannot be scored as is. Its climate, Redfin and Authority fields are null because of the planning-region mismatch (national counties).
  • Target revenue and headcount are often missing because ZoomInfo enrichment was unavailable (Punctual Pros add-on targets).
  • The revenue path to about $100M by month 36 is an assumption, not a forecast (est.).

Next actions

  1. Rank the 195 Phase 1 ZIP codes and the Phase 2 states using the national county table. Flag any county with null fields.
  2. Open founder conversations with the Ron Williams group and C&C first. Seventeen PE sponsors are competing for the same founders.
  3. Fill in revenue and headcount for the top 10 targets before the month-12 tuck-in checkpoint.
  4. Map the 54 unowned Authority territories to counties, so Phase 2 sequencing follows that density.

# Where Punctual Pros Should Expand First

Expand first into the counties next to the Central-PA core and the Jersey Shore beachhead, not into new national markets. The named targets point to Chester County, PA, New Castle County, DE, and Monmouth, Middlesex, Somerset, Union and Essex counties, NJ, with Worcester County, MD as a second step.

## Why stay close to home

- In the plan, Phase 1 (months 0-12) fills the 248-zip core and the 195 best nearby ZIP codes: 144 in PA and 51 in MD (Punctual Pros nationwide plan).
- Phase 2 (months 9-24) repeats the Horvath deal across PA, NJ, MD, DE and southern NY. That region holds 54 mapped Authority territories Punctual Pros does not yet own (Punctual Pros nationwide plan).
- Across sponsor cases, the first add-on came early and close to home, a median of about 7 months after entry. Tuck-ins then followed every three to five months (value creation cases).
- A national move comes last. Phase 4 means consolidating inside the One Hour / Ben Franklin / Mister Sparky system, where Punctual Pros holds about 2.3% of $831M reported revenue (Punctual Pros nationwide plan).

## First counties, by target

(Punctual Pros add-on targets)

- The Ron Williams group owns both West Chester and Delmarva. One deal could open Chester and Worcester counties (est.).
- Phase 3 metros come after these: Baltimore-DC, Richmond, the Philadelphia suburbs and Pittsburgh (Punctual Pros nationwide plan).

## What the data cannot yet show

- The national county table was generated Oct 6, 2026, but the context does not include its county rankings. A true nationwide ranking needs its demand, climate and Authority-density fields sorted by score.
- Connecticut cannot be scored as is. Its climate, Redfin and Authority fields are null because of the planning-region mismatch (national counties).
- Target revenue and headcount are often missing because ZoomInfo enrichment was unavailable (Punctual Pros add-on targets).
- The revenue path to about $100M by month 36 is an assumption, not a forecast (est.).

## Next actions

1. Rank the 195 Phase 1 ZIP codes and the Phase 2 states using the national county table. Flag any county with null fields.
2. Open founder conversations with the Ron Williams group and C&C first. Seventeen PE sponsors are competing for the same founders.
3. Fill in revenue and headcount for the top 10 targets before the month-12 tuck-in checkpoint.
4. Map the 54 unowned Authority territories to counties, so Phase 2 sequencing follows that density.
